compliance.emc: FCC Class A, ICES 003 Class A, AS/NZS 3548 Class A, CISPR 22 (EN55022) Class A, VCCI Class A, BSMI Class A
compliance.immunity: IEC/EN-61000-4-2 ESD (8 kV contact, 15 kV air), -4-3 radiated (10 V/m), -4-4 EFT (2 kV power, 1 kV signal), -4-5 surge (AC 4 kV CM / 2 kV DM, signal 1 kV, DC 1 kV), -4-6 conducted (10 Vrms), -4-8 power-frequency magnetic field (30 A/m), -4-11 dips and interruptions
compliance.nebs: designed to meet SR-3580 NEBS Criteria Level 3, GR-1089-CORE and GR-63-CORE
compliance.safety: UL/CSA/IEC/EN 60950-1, IEC/EN 60825 laser safety, ACA TS001, AS/NZS 60950

features.ethernet: 10-Gbps IEEE 802.3ae, 40/100-Gbps IEEE 802.3ba, 100GE PHY monitoring, IEEE 802.x flow control, full duplex, per-port byte and packet counters
features.timing: 2 x BITS RJ-45, ToD RJ-45, 10 MHz and 1 PPS SMB per RP, IEEE 1588 PTP telecom profiles G.8265.1/G.8275.1/G.8275.2 and SyncE

management.usb: 1 x USB class A per RP

performance.port-modes-qsfp28: 10, 40 and 100 Gigabit Ethernet - data sheet Table 2, "16 QSFP28 ports capable of 10Gb, 40Gb, and 100Gb Ethernet". Cisco publishes no per-optic list for this chassis and points at the Cisco Optics Compatibility Matrix instead, so this is the rate list and not an optics list
performance.port-modes-sfp-plus: 10 Gigabit Ethernet - data sheet Table 2, "20 SFP+ ports capable of 10Gb Ethernet", with no dual-rate note beside it. The chassis-wide sentence "10, 25, 40, 100, and 400 Gigabit Ethernet interface types across the ASR 9903 chassis" covers the Port Expansion Cards as well and is not a claim about these twenty cages

power.power-input-ac: 200-240 VAC high line, 90-130 VAC low line, 50-60 Hz
power.power-input-dc: -48 VDC nominal, -40.5 to -72 VDC, 40 A max per module
power.power-redundancy-ac: 2+2 at high line, 3+1 at low line

thermal.air-filter: ASR-9903-FILTER, one serviceable filter on the front

configs.description: The AC build: four PWR-1.6KW-AC modules. Named explicitly even though the base already seats them, so that asking for the AC variant does not mean knowing which flavour the base happens to carry. Redundancy is 2+2 at high line (200-240 V) and 3+1 at low line (90-130 V); a module handles both, but swapping between them means pulling the supply out and back in.
configs.name: ac

configs.description: Chassis only - what you spec before deciding what goes in it. Both route processors, four AC supplies and all four fan trays are seated; the Port Expansion Card bay is EMPTY, which is how the router ships when nobody orders a PEC. The thirty-six fixed-board ports are part of the chassis and are there in every configuration.
configs.name: base

configs.description: The DC build: four PWR-1.6KW-DC modules at -48 VDC, 2+2. The chassis PID is ASR-9903 either way; the supplies are separate line items. Mixing AC and DC modules in one chassis is not supported, which is why this is a configuration of the whole chassis rather than a choice per bay.
configs.name: dc

configs.description: With the 2T Port Expansion Card in bay 1 - five 400GE QSFP-DD and fifteen 100GE QSFP28 ports on top of the fixed board's thirty-six, for 3.6 Tbps. This is what the Visio master draws and what Figure 3 of the install guide photographs.
configs.name: pec-2t

configs.description: With the 800G Port Expansion Card in bay 1 - forty-eight SFP+ ports, of which thirty-two also run 25GE, grouped into slice 4 and slice 5.
configs.name: pec-800g

gaps.note: TWO CISCO DOCUMENTS GIVE THIS CHASSIS TWO MAXIMUM WEIGHTS and they are not reconcilable as different scopes. Table 2 of the ASR 9903 data sheet (c78-744035) reads "ASR 9903 chassis (including 2 RPs, 4 PSUs, 4 FANs): 5.18 x 17.475 x 30 in.; 81.62 lb (131.57 mm x 443.86 mm x 762 mm; 37 kg)". The fixed-port Hardware Installation Guide's Lifting Guidelines read "A fully-configured Cisco ASR 9903 can weigh as much as 70 pounds (31.75 kg)". Both are maxima and the guide's scope is the WIDER of the two - "fully configured" must include a PEC, which the data sheet's list does not - so the larger figure should have been the guide's, and it is 5.25 kg smaller. `chassis.weight-kg` carries the data sheet's 37 kg because the source table makes the data sheet authoritative for weight, and this gap carries the guide's figure so the disagreement is not silently resolved.
gaps.wanted: a scale under a real ASR 9903, or a Cisco document that states the weight with its scope spelled out.

gaps.note: The furniture strip at the right of the RP row carries four features. Two are identified and drawn: a hex grounding stud and an IEC 60417-5019 earth symbol. The other two are not. Above the stud the master draws a plain circular dimple about 3 mm across, and between them a smaller dark circle that reads as a through-hole on the install guide's Figure 3 render at 2.7 px/mm. NO SENTENCE IN THE INTAKE NAMES EITHER. They are the right shape and the right place for an ESD wrist-strap jack and a captive-screw well - the ASR 9001 has an ESD socket on its front and Figure 9 of the same guide points at it - but the ASR 9903 is not in that figure and the guide's ESD section names no socket for this chassis. Drawing them as an esd-jack would be a guess with a citation attached, so they are left off.
gaps.wanted: a callout in a Cisco figure, or a photograph of the front right corner close enough to read the two features.

gaps.note: The front master draws a recessed frame 13.51 x 26.01 mm at the left end of the fixed board with a yellow tag in it reading ATTENTION / ON-OFF, and the install guide's Figure 3 render shows the same recess with a plain white tag. WHAT IT IS, IS NOT SAID FOR THIS CHASSIS. The identical assembly on the ASR 9902's REAR is captioned in Figure 158 of the same guide with POWER printed under it and a lamp beside it, so on that chassis it is a power switch. For the ASR 9903 the guide says only "There is no power switch available on the AC and DC PSUs for the Cisco ASR 9903 routers as they are plug-and-play devices ... The power LED (PWR) is available on the front-side of the router", which places a PWR lamp on the front and names no switch. So the recess and its tag are drawn as panel decor and silkscreen, exactly as the artwork has them, and nothing here asserts that they are a switch.
gaps.wanted: a callout naming this feature on the ASR 9903, or a photograph of the front left corner.

gaps.note: FT0 to FT3 are printed on the chassis in a notch at the bottom left of each tray - the tray is cut away there and the label plate shows through, which is how the drawing and the guide's Figure 4 both have it. This model draws each tray as a filled rectangle, so the four marks land under their bays and L21 reports them. The marks are kept at the positions the master gives rather than moved somewhere they would render, because moving them would put ink where the device has none; the honest fix is a notched tray outline, which is a component change.
gaps.wanted: cisco/asr-9903-fan@1 drawn with its bottom-left notch, so the chassis label shows through it.

gaps.note: THE TOP, BOTTOM AND TWO SIDES ARE SIZED AND NOT DRAWN, and each carries an `empty:` sentence saying where the search ran. What they have in common is that no source in the intake ELEVATES them. The Visio stencil's 119 masters are front and rear elevations and hold no plan or side view at all. The install guide's figures for this chassis are two elevations, a top-view FOOTPRINT (Figure 19, which dimensions the outline and draws no feature), an airflow path, two rack-mounting sequences, a bracket-to-side sequence and an air-filter exploded view - the last two show the sides at an angle and dimension nothing on them. The data sheet gives the envelope. WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE, from the photographs, is a cisco wordmark and a large product label on the top, four feet and the bracket landings underneath, and a bracket rail on each side. None is positioned by anything, and drawing them by eye off a three-quarter render would put unmeasured furniture on four faces at once.
gaps.wanted: a Cisco mechanical drawing of the ASR 9903, or orthographic photographs of the top and one side with something of known size in frame.

gaps.note: NEITHER THE FAN TRAY NOR THE ROUTE PROCESSOR CARRIES A DRAW FIGURE MEASURED ON THIS CHASSIS, and the L27 and L29 warnings are left standing as the record. The one per-FRU table in the intake is a `show environment` example in the fixed-port guide's troubleshooting chapter, and it was taken on an ASR 9902: its rows read ASR-9902-LC 614/283, A99-RP-F 102/43 and ASR-9902-FAN 72/7. The RP figure is this chassis's RP and cisco/a99-rp-f@1 carries it. The fan row is a different tray in a 2RU chassis with three of them, and the PECs have no row at all because an ASR 9902 has no PEC bay. Searched: Table 35 of the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide (modular-chassis cards only), Table 24 of the Overview and Reference Guide (modular-chassis fan trays only), the ASR 9903 and ASR 9902 data sheets, and every document in the intake for "Power consumption" on a line with one of these part numbers.
gaps.wanted: a Cisco specifications appendix for the fixed-port chassis, or a `show environment` capture from a real ASR 9903.
the buried marks moved clear of the components that paint over them

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

`attrs.platform.cpu`, `attrs.platform.memory`; one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on port groups qsfp28, sfp-plus - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays
the Nautobot exporter is not importable - unlocks NetBox / Nautobot device-type export

air-filter.note: NOT DRAWN, deliberately. ASR-9903-FILTER mounts on the FRONT of the chassis, in front of every face this model draws - Figure 177, "Install Air Filter-Cisco ASR 9903", shows it sliding onto the front mounting brackets as a full-face frame. Drawing it would hide the whole front view, and it is an option rather than part of the chassis. ASR-9903-CAB-MGMT is left out for the reason the modelling guide gives for cable management generally: it is not a panel fact.

chassis.note: datasheet - Table 2 of c78-744035, "Physical dimensions (includes ejector bracket/lever); (H x W x D); weight": "ASR 9903 chassis (including 2 RPs, 4 PSUs, 4 FANs): 5.18 x 17.475 x 30 in.; 81.62 lb (131.57 mm x 443.86 mm x 762 mm; 37 kg)", with the note underneath: "Excluding ejector, the depth is 23.62 in/600 mm". DEPTH IS THE 600, NOT THE 762, and the difference is not an ejector in the ordinary sense - 162 mm is far too much for one. The data sheet's own overview paragraph settles which figure describes the box: "The compact size (depth is 600 mm), front-to-back airflow ... make this platform very efficient". So 600 mm is the chassis and 762 is the chassis plus whatever Cisco measures in front of and behind it; `chassis.depth` carries the former and the 762 is recorded in attrs.physical beside it rather than discarded. WIDTH IS THE BODY. 443.86 mm is 17.475 in, which is not the 19 in rack face, so this figure is already between the ear folds and L43 has nothing to catch. HEIGHT IS THE CHASSIS AS BUILT, NOT THE RACK ALLOCATION: 131.57 mm against 3 RU's 133.35, built 1.78 mm under its allocation for clearance, the same shortfall the ASR 9904, 9906 and 9910 show. The install guide's own sentence agrees to a tenth - "Cisco ASR 9903 Router is 5.25 inches (13.34 cm)" is the ALLOCATION quoted as the height, which is exactly the rounding trap to expect here, so the data sheet's 5.18 in is carried and the RU is carried separately rather than reconciled.

cooling.note: datasheet - "The Cisco ASR 9903 Router is a compact router that supports two redundant Route Processors (RP), two integrated switch fabrics, 4 AC or DC power supply modules, and 4 fans in redundant configuration", and Table 2's Redundancy row lists "Fan redundancy" with no ratio. Airflow is "Front to back" in the same table, and the install guide adds the filter: "The Cisco ASR 9903 and Cisco ASR 9902 Router have a serviceable air filter (Cisco PID: ASR-9903-FILTER and ASR-9902-FILTER). The air filter is a single component. It removes dust from the room air drawn into the chassis by the fan trays." THE REDUNDANCY RATIO IS NOT PUBLISHED AND IS NOT SUPPLIED. Cisco names the property and not the arithmetic, so the `fan-trays` group carries a `redundancy-note` and NO `redundancy`, and L69 warns that this chassis does not say how many fans it can lose. That warning is the record. Four trays described as redundant is 3+1 or 2+2, the difference is the whole question a reader would be asking, and writing either would make a guess comparable with the ASR 9006's stated form. It is the ruling edgecore/csr310 already carries for "Hot swappable redundant fan modules", applied to a vendor who said more and still not enough.

face-check.note: done BEFORE measuring, because Cisco's master filenames name the wrong faces on the ASR 9910 and nothing downstream would have caught it. No swap here. "ASR-9903 Front" carries the two A99-RP-F cards, the fixed board's thirty-six ports numbered 0 to 35, the CISCO and ASR 9903 branding and the A9903-20HG-PEC in the lower bay, and matches Figure 3 of the install guide, "Front Panel of the Cisco ASR 9903 Router". "ASR-9903 Rear" carries the four power modules, the four FAN-ASR9903-V01 trays and the grounding panel, and matches Figure 4, "Rear Panel of the Cisco ASR 9903 Router".

fixed-board.note: THE FIXED BOARD IS NOT A BAY. The install guide's overview is explicit: "Fixed Board - also known as a Line Card (LC0). The Fixed Board contains sixteen 100GE QSFP28 ports and twenty 10GE SFP+ ports. It is integrated with the chassis and provides up to 1.6-Tbps throughput." So its thirty-six ports are placements on the chassis face, not a module's own, and there is nothing to seat or remove. THE NUMBERING IS THE GUIDE'S, NOT AN INFERENCE. Figure 120, "Cisco ASR 9903 Fixed Ports", labels callout 1 "QSFP28 ports (0-15)" and callout 2 "SFP+ ports (16-35)", and the master prints all thirty-six numerals under the cages - 0 and 1 under the first QSFP28 cage, 34 and 35 under the last SFP+ column - so the two readings confirm each other digit for digit. WITHIN A COLUMN, THE TRIANGLE SAYS WHICH IS WHICH. Each numeral has a small solid triangle beside it: a down-pointing one for the upper port and an up-pointing one for the lower, which is Cisco's usual marking on a stacked cage. Even numbers take the down triangle throughout, so the upper row is 0, 2, 4 ... 34 and the lower is 1, 3, 5 ... 35. THE APERTURES ARE THE STANDARD ONES. The master draws the QSFP28 bores at 19.02 x 8.92 mm against std/qsfp-ganged's 18.5 x 9.58, on a 29.17 mm column pitch and a 16.68 mm row pitch; the SFP+ bores are the module mouths rather than the cage openings, so those ports are positioned on their measured 14.36 mm column pitch and 10.71 mm row pitch, which sit within 0.8 and 3.0 percent of std/sfp-ganged's own 14.25 and 10.40. Placements are centred on the drawn bores in both cases.

grounding.note: install guide for what it is, master for where. "Cisco ASR 9902 and Cisco ASR 9903 Router - One grounding lug, which has two M5 bolt holes", and Figure 75, "NEBS Bonding and Grounding Points on the Cisco ASR 9903 Router", circles that lug on the fixed panel between the middle pair of fan trays. The rear master draws the two holes 15.77 mm apart on centres, which cisco/a9k-ground-pad@1's 15.3 mm two-hole lug covers to within half a millimetre; the pad is placed rotate: 90 because this chassis mounts the lug upright where the modular chassis mount it flat. A SECOND EARTH MARK IS ON THE FRONT and is drawn rather than documented. The front master prints a hex nut and an IEC 60417-5019 earth symbol on the furniture strip at the right of the RP row, and the install guide's grounding chapter describes only the rear lug. The symbol is placed where the drawing puts it and the stud beside it is panel decor; neither is claimed to be a second NEBS bonding point.

port-lamps.note: drawing for the count and the positions, install guide for the states. THIRTY-SIX LAMPS FOR THIRTY-SIX PORTS, one each, all on one baseline at y 84.48 and all cut to 2.80 x 1.60 mm - the master draws them as a single rounded rectangle beside each port's direction triangle. The rule reaches the end of the face: the last SFP+ port, 35, has its lamp at 426.74 like every other, and no port on this board is without one. THE STATES ARE TABLE 27 of the install guide, "Port Status and LC FAIL LEDs", transcribed: "Port Status LEDs (one per port). Green - Port state is up and a valid physical layer link is established. Blinking - Line activity is occurring. The LED blinks green-amber-green. Red - Port state is up, but there is a link loss or SFP/QSFP failure. Off - Port is administratively shut down." The blinking state is carried as a green lamp with an amber second colour, which is what "green-amber-green" describes.

port-modes.note: READ WHAT THE COLOURED CHIPS ARE. The master prints a dark red chip under port 10 and a cyan chip under port 14, a cyan band under ports 16 to 25 and a dark red band under 26 to 35, and a rate legend over each: "100G/-" over port 14's chip, "-/10G" over each SFP+ band. THE PAIRING IS THE DRAWING'S OWN DEVICE and the counts close. Table 2 of the data sheet gives the board three combinations - "16x100GE, 15x100GE + 10x10GE or 14x100GE + 20x10GE" - so each ten-port SFP+ block costs exactly one QSFP28 port, and the drawing says which two by colouring them to match: cyan port 14 against the cyan block 16-25, dark red port 10 against the dark red block 26-35. The legends read the same way, one slash-separated pair per mode. WHAT IS NOT SOURCED IS THE MAPPING IN WORDS. No sentence in the intake names ports 10 and 14 as the two that give way; the reading is the colour pairing plus the arithmetic, and it is recorded here rather than asserted in the configurations, which carry only what the data sheet states.

power.note: datasheet - Table 2 of c78-744035: "1.6 kW DC power module (up to 4 modules), redundancy: 2+2" and "1.6 kW AC power module (up to 4 modules), redundancy: AC high line (200-240V): 2+2; AC low line (90-130V): 3+1", with "Mixing of AC and DC modules is not supported". THE CHASSIS CARRIES NO ENVELOPE FIGURE AND THIS FILE INVENTS NONE. Neither the data sheet nor the install guide states a typical or maximum chassis draw for the ASR 9903; the closest thing in the intake is a `show environment` example in the troubleshooting chapter taken on an ASR 9902, which is a different chassis with two supplies and three fans. So there is no power-max-w here, the module contracts carry their own figures, and the L29 census counts what is missing rather than a number somebody guessed.

rp-lamp-count.note: A DISCREPANCY WORTH KNOWING ABOUT BEFORE SOMEBODY RE-COUNTS. Callout 1 of Figure 11 reads "10MHz and 1PPS ports / Eight discrete LED indicators", and the route processor's faceplate prints NINE legends: ACTIVE, FAIL, BOOT, SYNC and CRIT on one line, PWR, SSD, GPS and MAJ/MIN below. The ninth is almost certainly MAJ/MIN being counted as one lamp serving two alarm levels or being read as a legend rather than a lamp; nothing in the guide says which. The lamps belong to cisco/a99-rp-f@1 and this model does not restate them - the note is here because this file cites Figure 11 for the RP's ports, and a reader following that citation should know the same callout under-counts by one.

rp-slots.note: READ THIS BEFORE CHANGING THE RP BAY WIDTH. The two RP slots are on a 211.44 mm pitch and the bays carry that figure, while the module they accept, cisco/a99-rp-f@1, declares 221.84 mm. L33 reports the 10.40 mm difference and it is not a mistake in either number. THE PITCH IS MEASURED THREE WAYS AND ALL THREE AGREE. On the front master every feature of RP1 sits exactly 211.43 to 211.44 mm left of the matching feature on RP2 - the yellow A99-RP-F band at 16.38 against 227.81, the SYNC0 legend at 63.84 against 275.28, MGT LAN 0 at 129.43 against 340.87, and eighteen more. On the install guide's Figure 3 render, calibrated at 2.698 px/mm off the PEC plate's known 436.58 mm width, the two RPs' SYNC0 jack bezels sit 571 px apart, which is 211.7 mm. And the arithmetic closes across the face: 4.45 mm of left margin, two slots of 211.44, and a 16.5 mm furniture strip at the right carrying the grounding stud sums to 443.83 against a 443.86 body. WHAT THE 221.84 IS. The a99-rp-f master's art includes a retention bracket at each end, each about 11 mm wide with one captive screw, and its Visio shape box measures the lot. In the chassis those brackets INTERLEAVE - the screw on RP1's right bracket sits low and the screw on RP2's left bracket sits high, which is why the seam in the artwork shows two screws stacked in one bracket's width - so two cards on a 211.44 pitch is physically what the drawing shows, and the two plates overlap by 10.4 mm in the master because the artist pasted each card at its own full extent. SO THE BAY STAYS AT THE PITCH. docs/bay-and-component-size.md: "A bay may be larger than the cage opening (ejectors) but must NEVER be larger than the slot pitch", because widening past it makes adjacent bays overlap, which is what L13 reports. Two bays of 221.84 on a 211.44 pitch is exactly that. The component's figure is left alone rather than reconciled, per the same note's rule, and cisco/a99-rp-f@1's own size provenance should be re-read against this measurement - roc-ops/Portrayal#262 is where that belongs, not here.

sources.note: the Cisco ASR 9903 Compact High-Performance Router Data Sheet (c78-744035, 2021); the Cisco ASR 9000 Series Fixed-Port Routers Hardware Installation Guide (b-asr9001-hardware-installation-guide.pdf, last modified 2021-07-30, which despite its filename covers the 9001, 9901, 9902 and 9903); the Interface and Hardware Component Configuration Guide, IOS XR 24.x; and Cisco's own Visio stencil Routers-Cisco_ASR_9000, masters "ASR-9903 Front" and "ASR-9903 Rear". THE STENCIL IS THE GEOMETRY AND THE GUIDE IS THE IDENTITY of everything on the two faces; where they were compared, they agree.

stencil-calibration.note: THE TWO AXES AGREE TO 0.32 PERCENT, which is this stencil's trustworthy band - better than the ASR 9001's 0.66 and short of the ASR 9904's 0.06. The ink bounding box of both masters is the 19.0 in rack face flange-tip to flange-tip and the shape box in index.json reads exactly 1.9 x 0.525 in at 1:10, i.e. 482.60 x 133.35 mm, which is 19 in by 3 RU. Calibrating x on 482.60 over 1709.10 art units gives 0.282374 mm/unit and y on 133.35 over 473.75 units gives 0.281477 - 0.32 percent apart, so the drawing is uniform and the box is the rack face rather than the body. THE MODEL IS THEN ANCHORED ON THE BODY, not on the rack face, because the body is what the views are. The chassis metal inside the flanges spans 1569.68 units across and 469.25 down; setting those to the data sheet's 443.86 x 131.57 gives 0.282773 and 0.280384 mm/unit, which reproduces the rack-face calibration to 0.15 percent across and 0.39 percent down. Both calibrations are recorded because either can be re-derived from the other; the numbers in this file are the second. CONFIRMED ON SOMETHING NEVER USED AS AN INPUT, which is the check the ASR 9006's power shelf earned: the Port Expansion Card plate measures 3.26 mm from the body's left edge and 3.42 mm from its right. Nothing in the calibration forced that symmetry, and it holds to 0.16 mm.

unmodelled-front-furniture.note: TWO SMALL ROUND FEATURES ON THE FRONT RIGHT STRIP ARE NOT MODELLED AND ARE NOT GUESSED AT. Above the grounding stud the master draws a plain dimple and, below it, a dark slot; the same two appear on the install guide's Figure 3 render at 2.7 px/mm, where the upper reads as a blind dimple and the lower as a through-hole. Nothing in the guide names either. They could be an ESD strap jack and a captive-screw well, and calling them so would be a guess with a citation, so they are left off the face and recorded in a gap instead.
